chunks: Abū ‘Abdil Raḥmān Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad Al-‘Askari narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father ‘Ali, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abil Bilād, from one of our companions whose name was Ḥusain, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said:

The prayer is established in full form in three locations: in the Masjid Al-Ḥarām, in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and next to the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him).

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Where can prayers be performed in full form according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* elevates the shrine of Imam Ḥusain (a.s.) to the same legal status as the two primary sanctuaries of Islam, granting visitors the privilege of performing complete (tamm) prayers rather than the shortened (qasr) form typically required for travelers. This ruling underscores the unique spiritual authority (wilayah) of the Ahl al-Bayt, positioning their resting places as centers of divine presence where the distinction between local and traveler prayer is suspended. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing the Imams' shrines not merely as burial sites but as active nodes of spiritual connectivity comparable to the Kaaba and the Prophet’s Mosque.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Abū ‘Abdil Raḥmān Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad Al-‘Askari narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from his father ‘Ali, from Ḥusain ibn Sa’īd, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abil Bilād, from one of our companions whose name was Ḥusain, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
You can establish (the obligatory) prayers in full form in three locations: in Masjid Al-Ḥarām, in the Mosque of the Messenger (s.a.a.w.), and next to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.).
